\section*{AP \({ }^{\text {® }}\) CALCULUS AB \\ 2007 SCORING GUIDELINES (Form B)}

\section*{Question 5}

Consider the differential equation \(\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{1}{2} x+y-1\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] On the axes provided, sketch a slope field for the given differential equation at the nine points indicated.
(Note: Use the axes provided in the exam booklet.)
\item[(b)] Find \(\frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}}\) in terms of \(x\) and \(y\). Describe the region in the \(x y\)-plane in which all solution curves to the differential equation are concave up.
\item[(c)] Let \(y=f(x)\) be a particular solution to the differential equation with the initial condition \(f(0)=1\). Does \(f\) have a relative minimum, a relative maximum, or neither at \(x=0\) ? Justify your answer.
\item[(d)] Find the values of the constants \(m\) and \(b\), for which \(y=m x+b\) is a solution to the differential equation.
\item[(a)]
![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/8713a368-82b8-4b2f-8c0e-44f18d052280-1.jpg?height=404&width=389&top_left_y=1195&top_left_x=647)
\item[(b)] \(\frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}}=\frac{1}{2}+\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{1}{2} x+y-\frac{1}{2}\)
\end{itemize}
Solution curves will be concave up on the half-plane above the line \(y=-\frac{1}{2} x+\frac{1}{2}\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(c)] \(\left.\frac{d y}{d x}\right|_{(0,1)}=0+1-1=0\) and \(\left.\frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}}\right|_{(0,1)}=0+1-\frac{1}{2}>0\)
Thus, \(f\) has a relative minimum at (0, 1).
\item[(d)] Substituting \(y=m x+b\) into the differential equation:
\[
m=\frac{1}{2} x+(m x+b)-1=\left(m+\frac{1}{2}\right) x+(b-1)
\]
Then \(0=m+\frac{1}{2}\) and \(m=b-1: m=-\frac{1}{2}\) and \(b=\frac{1}{2}\).
\item[2] : Sign of slope at each point and relative steepness of slope lines in rows and columns.
\item[3] : \(\left\{\begin{array}{l}2: \frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}} \\ 1: \text { description }\end{array}\right.\)
\item[] \(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { answer } \\ 1: \text { justification }\end{array}\right.\)
\item[] \(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { value for } m \\ 1: \text { value for } b\end{array}\right.\)
\end{itemize}
